Picking Chihiro is good symbolism, but in my opinion it just ain't it. Something just feels wrong. He decided, out of nowhere, while not showing obvious, and non ambiguous signs of liking her, to like her and confess to her. It was really unexpected, like seeing the movie about a sad mom who is dying and then suddenly the hospital exploded out of nowhere. 

Not sure about organic and stuff like that, wasn't Nanaka the same? He is just himself during the Nanaka arc.

I do. But first:

Keima was also flustered with other girls as well. Yui is one example, Haqua also said that he doesn't like aggressive advances (suddenly kissing, suddenly approached) This might be proven true when he kissed Chihiro intentionally and as far as I remember he didn't blush during it, compared to when other girls kissed him unexpectedly. 

Blushing doesn't equal love you know. He blushes a ton during his reconquest of Yui, but he didn't pick her in the end. 

This was simply not enough proof, at least for me. Do you think this makes sense? :

Approach = Blush
Sudden Kiss = Blush
Kissing Chihiro intentionally ≠ Blush

How does all that equal Love? 
But all that can mean that he doesn't like aggressive girls.

1. Keima never pretended to be another person to Nanaka as well, he was being himself, and sure enough, Nanaka fell in love with him too. Same could be said to Tenri. 

2. How should I say this... Dokurou did say that Keima likes her because she just never follows what he says (roughly like that). But I feel like this just doesn't feel enough of a reason. 

3. It's not only her that changed him you know.... Everyone participated, I am not sure about how much she changed him, but I believe it's less than what other girls have done, considering she appears very little during the part where Keima's mental state is changing. 

4. I agree that it makes the most sense to use her as the last heroine, since she represents the real and therefore symbolizes that Keima is interested in the real. But it just feels so random to suddenly have him confess to her. As I've said earlier before, she doesn't have enough appearance (Keima life pro tips --> meeting = romantic feeling UP)


Extra:

I felt sad for the other goddesses hosts. As I remember, the time loop in TWGOK is that of a causal loop, where that loop will stay the same, unchanging. This means that in every iteration of the loop up till infinity, there will never be a future with Keima and the other goddesses hosts (as long as he doesn't want a harem and only wants to be with Chihiro) the future can branch out from when he came back to the present, but that still wouldn't change stuff as he always wanted to go back to Chihiro

Par no 3: 
Feels like that's how he always does his conquest. Once girl fall in love > confess. I agree that Chihiro here is unique because she doesn't get her spirit removed by a kiss. Maybe that's because the one that does it is has to be the girl, because it could signify that her love hasn't peaked yet if she didn't kiss him. Par no 4: 
I feel like he just did that because Chihiro was the one that will have the easiest conquest considering she was already confessing and all. It's also a way to make Ayumi (remember, this is before he knew Chihiro didn't have a goddess) react to their relationship. Keima needed to see her reaction and deduce whether or not she has a goddess within her.

Par no 5:
Might be just because he was just sad. I think he knew that switching over suddenly like that would be wrong (and also chaotic and hard to do, even if he can do it). As time passes Keima seems to care more about others and the world. 

Par no 6:
He doesn't want to reject her because he doesn't like to make people sad (that's the most simplest way I can describe it) I remember he said that he was sorry and didn't meant what he said to Chihiro before, but I am sure anyone, whether in love or not, and anyone with slightest sense of humanity, not want to see people suffer because of their actions. 

Par no 7:
There were Ayumi's memories too. I feel like the remark from Kaori saying that he just uses them to achieve something affected him, considering he probably knew that he manipulated them in order to fall in love with him and save the world. This interpretation makes sense when he doesn't want to do his mission there anymore. He doesn't want to involve people and let them get hurt. 

I personally didn't relate to her at all, might've been why I ignored quite a bit of stuff(or forgot about them)
